title: Report: Ubisoft is pushing for generative AI to be deeply integrated into its game development process; projects that do not introduce AI must declare the reason
excerpt: When pitching a new game project at Ubisoft, the greenlight materials now include a required question: What can generative AI do for you? According to a Novembe
content_html:
When pitching a new game project at Ubisoft, the greenlight materials now include a required question: What can generative AI do for you? According to a November 26 report by the outlet Vertical Slice, Ubisoft is pushing hard to deeply integrate generative AI into its game development pipeline—when teams submit new project proposals, they must explain how AI can help development; those who do not plan to use it must clearly explain why to senior management.

If the Reasons Aren’t Convincing, Proposals Struggle to Pass

Multiple employees revealed that if a proposal does not involve generative AI and the reasons given to executives are not convincing enough, it is very difficult to get approved. An anonymous employee relayed management’s logic: AI can speed up how small, lean, and agile teams submit proposals. The company wants teams to move quickly, iterate repeatedly, cut unsuitable projects in time, and identify ideas with real potential. In other words, AI is being treated internally at Ubisoft as an accelerator for filtering ideas—whether you use it or not, you first have to give an explanation.

Pushing AI Amid a Restructuring Wave Deals Another Blow to Morale

The push goes beyond process. Over the past year or so, Ubisoft has continued large-scale restructuring: setting up new subsidiaries, integrating major game brands such as Assassin’s Creed, Far Cry, and Rainbow Six into different creative divisions, while also closing some studios and going through multiple rounds of layoffs. One employee described the company as sinking into a top-down “AI mania nightmare” pushed by management—internal morale was already low, and CEO Yves Guillemot has bet the company’s future on this technology and is demanding that other employees follow that direction. Having to answer the AI question first when seeking project approval is exactly how this strategy lands on every team’s desk as part of daily work.
